claims.claim: RTX sits on a defense-production bottleneck where sustained procurement demand requires converting contracted missile demand into supplier, workforce, facility and production throughput; rising deliveries provide evidence that some conversion is occurring.
The successor bottleneck is distributed industrial capacity across hundreds of suppliers rather than demand alone, making resilience dependent on supplier throughput and production-system investment.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Long-duration missile frameworks and contracts position RTX at a constrained defense-production node.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Capacity investment is explicit, but throughput depends on hundreds of suppliers, workforce and facilities.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Contracted demand supports visibility, while procurement continuity and supplier execution remain external dependencies.

risks.risk: A constrained supplier base can keep production below contracted or targeted rates even when end demand is strong.

causalEdges.mechanism: multi-year government frameworks create sustained requirements for precision munitions
causalEdges.falsifier: procurement priorities or budgets materially reverse

causalEdges.mechanism: workforce, facilities, technology and supplier throughput convert contracts into units
causalEdges.falsifier: supplier/facility constraints prevent sustained production-rate increases

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not quantify supplier-specific bottlenecks or full production-rate economics.

claims.claim: Long-duration contracts reduce demand uncertainty but do not remove production, supplier, cost or procurement-policy risk.
Higher deliveries validate some execution; they should not be inflated into proof that targeted production rates, margins or supplier resilience are already achieved.

factors.name: concentrationRisk
factors.basis: Defense production depends materially on government procurement continuity and program priorities.

factors.name: supplyChainRisk
factors.basis: RTX explicitly identifies the need for investment across hundreds of suppliers, workforce and facilities.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Delivery growth is observable, while future rate targets and economics remain prospective.

risks.risk: Supplier or facility bottlenecks can prevent contracted demand from converting to timely deliveries.
Government budget or program-priority changes can alter demand despite current frameworks.

causalEdges.mechanism: throughput, input costs and funded quantities determine whether backlog converts into profitable deliveries
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained delivery-rate increases and stable economics demonstrate resilient conversion

contradictions.claim: Strong contracted demand versus constrained production system
contradictions.resolution: The tension is structural rather than contradictory: demand visibility is high precisely while industrial capacity remains a limiting factor.

unknowns.unknown: Segment margin impact and supplier-level concentration are not established by the reused evidence.
